title: ClientFrame
description:
What a client sends the host daemon over its unix socket (R-PROTO-1's
second transport), one JSON object a line. The first line is `hello`;
everything after it wraps the same `Command` the in-process client
hands `Host::execute`, so a client is written once for both.

oneOf.description:
Names the protocol the client speaks, and the directory a new
session it starts runs in: the daemon serves every directory at once.

krowkVersion.description: The client's own version, for the daemon's log.

answersApprovals.description:
Whether the client answers `approval.requested` (an interactive client). A turn
it runs asks it, and a request left with no such client
following the session is denied. One that does not (`gruntas -p`)
runs its turns as the in-process `-p` does: what would be asked
is refused, with what would allow it.

token.description:
The daemon's bearer token (`host.token`, beside the socket): what
a WebSocket client proves it is this user with, since TCP cannot
say whose process connected. It rides the hello rather than a
header because browsers and Workers cannot set headers on a
WebSocket. The unix socket ignores it: its permissions already
keep everyone else out.

background.description:
A client that never holds the daemon up: the idle exit and `stop`
do not count it (an automatic sync bridge).

oneOf.description:
Runs a command; answered by `done` with the same `id`. The session a
`prompt` or `continue` runs in is followed from its first line.

clientRef.description:
The client's own name for this command (a uuid), on a prompt
that starts a session: a connection cut before its first line
named the session finds it again by this (`attach.clientRef`).
Kept by the daemon for 10 minutes.

oneOf.description:
Follows a session: what its log holds after `afterEventId` (all of
it when absent), the running turn's frames so far, then every frame
as it happens — the same ones each other client following it gets.
Answered by `attached` once the catching-up is sent.

afterSeq.description:
The last `line.seq` of this session the client has: of the
running turn's frames, only later ones are sent, so a client
resuming from its cursor sees nothing twice.

epoch.description:
The daemon's `welcome.epoch` the client's `afterSeq` is from. A
`seq` is a daemon's own: one from another daemon, or with no
epoch, is not honoured, and the client is caught up from
`afterEventId` alone.

clientRef.description:
Follows, from its start, the session the `execute` with this
`clientRef` started, in place of `sessionId` (sent empty): a
prompt whose connection was cut before its first line. Answered
once the prompt has named its session; with its error when it
ended without one, and `bad_session` when the daemon has no such
prompt.

oneOf.description: Asks how the daemon is; answered by `status`.

Asks the pairing this host opened because a new machine signed in
to the person's account: answered by `pairingOffer`, with none when
there is no such pairing.

The person's yes or no to adding the new machine a `pairingOffer`
named at the `confirm` stage; answered by `done`, with
`no_pairing_offer` when none waits for an answer.
`pairing` is the offer's own, so a yes meant for one pairing is never
taken for the next.

Asks the MCP servers of a session, as its host holds them; answered
by `mcp`, with none for a session that has no servers. Protocol 3.

Starts one of a session's MCP servers again at once; answered by
`done`, with `no_such_server` when the session has no such server. It
connects in the background: ask `mcpStatus` to see. Protocol 3.

Begins signing in to one of a session's MCP servers, on the host that
holds its connections (so the tokens land where calls are made);
answered by `mcpSignIn`, or `done` with the reason it could not begin.
Protocol 3.

Finishes the sign-in `mcpSignInStart` began, with the address the
browser landed on: a secret, never logged. Answered by `done`.
Protocol 3.

Signs one of a session's MCP servers out: its tokens are removed and
its connection closed. Answered by `done`, with `no_such_server` when
the session has no such server. Protocol 3.

Something a session of a harness gruntas does not run itself (Claude
Code, Codex) did, as its plugin's hook (`gruntas hook`) tells it:
answered by `activity`. Taken only on the unix socket. Protocol 3: a
daemon that does not know it skips the line and answers nothing.

Reads the instances again — config.json and the credentials file —
for every host, after a client connected or signed one out
(`gruntas connect`): `changed` is that instance, whose backend processes are
not reused; `renamedFrom` and `renamedTo` a rename, whose are.
Answered by `done` once applied; a command sent after it runs on
what it read, answered or not.

Asks the daemon to exit — `gruntas host stop`, or `gruntas machines always-on on`
handing over to the service. Refused with `host_busy` while a turn
runs, and with `host_in_use` while another client is connected
unless `force` (an interactive client connected to it reconnects to the next one);
answered by `done` just before it goes.

Stops following a session: the client moved to another
session. Its frames no longer come, and a request only this
client could have answered is denied.

Command.description:
What a client asks of the engine. `prompt`, `interrupt`, `steer`,
`approve`, `switchModel` and `continue` are served today; the rest are typed now so
every client is written against the whole vocabulary, and are refused
with `not_implemented` until their tickets land.

oneOf.description: Start a turn: in `sessionId` when given, else in a new session.

images.description: The images the text names by `[Image #N]`.

model.description: The model for this turn; the session's last one when absent.

toolset.description:
The toolset preset for this turn (`claude`, `gpt`, `grok`); the
config's, else the one the model's family picks, when absent.

effort.description:
The reasoning effort for this turn, on gruntas's ladder; the
instance's, else the provider's default, when absent.

rollover.description:
What a limited turn does for this session (`--rollover`); it
replaces the session's recorded value. When absent, the session's
recorded value, else the repository's and the global config's.

budget.description:
The spend this session, with its subagents, may reach: the engine
refuses the model call that would go past it (R-BUDGET-1). No
limit when absent.

attendance.description:
For a prompt that starts a session: whether a person is at it,
recorded in its start record. Ignored for an existing session.

origin.description:
Where the prompt came from. For one that starts a session, an
agent origin's `sessionId` is recorded as the new session's
parent.

oneOf.description:
Keep one image's bytes on the host, ahead of the `prompt` or `steer`
that names it by `sha256`: the host accepts it only when the hash
matches the bytes, the format is png, jpeg, gif or webp and it is at
most 2.75 MiB, and a repeat of a hash it holds succeeds without
writing. With no `sessionId` (a prompt that will start a session) the
image waits for that prompt. One image a message, so none goes over
a transport's 4 MiB cap. Protocol 2.
Stop the running turn, keeping what it produced so far.

origin.description: Where the command came from; absent when the sender did not say.

oneOf.description:
Add input to the running turn without stopping it. The engine takes
it before its next model call, and it is logged there as a
`userText` item.

origin.description: Where the command came from; absent when the sender did not say.

oneOf.description:
Answer an `approval.requested`: for one with `questions`, `allow`
with the person's `answers`.

origin.description: Where the command came from; absent when the sender did not say.

oneOf.description:
Continue the session on another model, instance or engine
(R-SWITCH-4): checked now — the instance, its key or login, its
binary — and refused with the fix when it cannot run, the session
staying where it was; accepted, it is logged as `model.switched` and
the session's next prompt runs there. While a turn runs it is logged
once the turn is over. Without `sessionId` it is only checked: a
client that has no session yet asks before its first prompt.

origin.description: Where the command came from; absent when the sender did not say.

oneOf.description:
Branch the session at an event: the new branch's first event names
it as its parent.

Run the turn a backend began by itself (`turn.unprompted`) — Claude
Code answering a background agent that finished — as a turn of the
session, logged like any other. Refused with `nothing_pending` when
no such turn is waiting. A `prompt` that arrives first runs it ahead
of itself, so no prompt ever ends at that turn's answer.

ImageInput.description:
An image as a client sends it with a prompt or a steer, and the number
its `[Image #N]` in the text carries. Either its bytes (`data`, which the
engine keeps beside the session's log), or, since protocol 2, only its
`sha256` and no `data`: the bytes went ahead in a `putImage`, and the
host refuses the prompt when it holds none by that name.

data.description: The bytes, base64. Empty when the image is named by `sha256` alone.

sha256.description: The sha256 of the bytes, lowercase hex. Required when `data` is empty.

ModelRef.description:
A model, named as the instance that serves it and the provider's own id
for it: `{"instance": "anthropic", "model": "claude-opus-5-5"}`.

instance.description: A name from the instance registry, e.g. `anthropic` or `anthropic:work`.

PermissionMode.description:
Claude-Code-compatible permission modes (R-PERM-1): `default` asks
before edits and commands, `acceptEdits` before commands, `plan` changes
nothing, and `bypassPermissions` asks before nothing — though a deny
rule, an ask rule and a hook's ask still hold in each of those. gruntas's
own `unhinged` holds nothing gruntas's rules say: every call runs but one a
hook blocks (`crate::permissions`).

Effort.description:
How hard a model thinks, on one ladder for every provider (R-PROV-2).
Each model takes some of these rungs under its own names; the rung asked
for is mapped onto the nearest one the model takes (`crate::effort`).

Rollover.description:
What happens when a session's instance hits its rate or usage limit
(R-INST-7, R-INST-8, R-ROLL-4): the session's own value, else the
repository's when it is trusted, else the global config's, else `offer`.

oneOf.description: Ask, one keystroke, never silently: the default.
Move to the next instance without asking.
Fail the turn: no offer, and no hint to continue elsewhere.

BudgetLimits.description:
What a session may spend, counted over the session and every subagent
it spawned, from the usage the provider metered — never from what a
request asked for.

maxTokens.description:
Generated tokens — output and reasoning, the part that overshoots a
request's cap: `--max-tokens`.

Attendance.description:
Whether a person is at a session: the start path that makes the session
records it, never inferred from other flags (such as whether the client
answers approvals). Unattended is a session gruntas started headless on
someone's behalf — a launcher worker, a session a host command starts
(`sync new --host`, delegation), `-p` without a terminal; every other
session is attended. A session whose record says nothing (an older
gruntas started it) counts as attended.

Origin.description:
Where a steering command came from (D7): the channel it arrived through,
the only signal used. Every command that acts on a session other than
the caller's own — a prompt to an existing session, `steer`, `interrupt`,
`approve`, `switchModel`, and `take` — carries one when its sender knows
it; a command without one (an older client's) has an unknown origin.

sessionId.description:
The session the command came from, when `kind` is `agent`. On a
prompt that starts a new session, the new session's parent.

device.description:
The name of the machine the command was sent from. Absent only
where the sender's name is not at hand: a host command carries just
the sending session.

attendance.description:
Whether the steering session is attended, when `kind` is `agent` and
the sender knows it (its own session's start record says): the host
holds a steering session it has no log of to this word, since the
session may run on another machine. Absent: attended.

OriginKind.description: Who a steering command came from.

ApprovalDecision.description:
An answer to a permission request: allow this call, allow calls like it
for the rest of the session or for good in this project (the request's
`remember` rules), or deny it.

QuestionAnswer.description:
The person's answer to one question: the labels of the options picked,
and what they wrote, if anything. Neither means they left it unanswered.

Activity.description:
What a session gruntas does not run did, one `activity` frame each:
registering at its start, leaving at its end, a heavy command starting
and ending, a turn's end, a permission prompt and other activity, and
its account's usage windows.

oneOf.description:
A session started (or resumed): the daemon keeps it until it ends or
its harness process is gone.
A session ended.
A command on the heavy list started, as tool call `toolCallId`.
And ended.

A turn of the session ended: the heavy commands it had not ended
count no more. Answered with `reportDue` when it did work it has
not reported.

A tool call of the session ended (`PostToolUse`): work its agent
has not reported yet. Not sent for the report tool's own call.

The session's agent reported its status (`gruntas_report`, D2):
answered with the session's Task as it now stands, or
`not_registered`. The daemon stamps it with its own clock.

A permission prompt waits on the person: the session is
input-required until its next activity (D3).

The session did something the daemon keeps nothing else of (a tool
call off the heavy list, a refused permission): its last activity,
and the end of a permission prompt.

`gruntas run claude --unattended` started a background session
(`claude --bg`): the daemon keeps it and stops it (`<program> stop
<id>` under its config home) once its Task is terminal and its turn
has ended.

id.description: The id `claude --bg` printed: the first part of its session id.

configHome.description:
The account's config home (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`); none is
Claude Code's own default.

oneOf.description: An account's usage windows, as its harness reads them.

PluginHarness.description: A harness whose sessions gruntas's plugin reports from.

Registration.description:
A session of a harness gruntas does not run, as the daemon knows it.
Everything past the id and the harness is what its hook could tell.

sessionId.description: The harness's own id for it.

harnessPid.description: The harness's process: the entry goes when it is gone.

configHome.description: The account it runs as, by its config home.

repository.description: The working directory's repository, as its origin remote's URL.

Report.description:
One `gruntas_report` (D2), as its history entry records it; the summary
is the message's text.

timestamp.description: When it was reported, RFC 3339, the publishing machine's clock.

TaskState.description:
A2A's `TaskState`, as ProtoJSON writes it. A state this build does not
know reads as `Unspecified`, rather than refusing the whole board.

UsageWindow.description: One of an account's usage windows: the 5-hour or the 7-day.

usedPercent.description: How much of it is used, 0 to 100.

resetsAtMs.description: When it resets, in ms since the epoch.
